hypothesis: An experience-trained source-native learner can infer unknown non-affine causal parent sets from interleaved public interventions and preserve multiple unfamiliar worlds, composing future actions; compare an equally informed independently written exhaustive three-parent truth-table estimator.
source: Eight-bit opaque public state, three public actions, each output bit derives a seeded unknown Boolean truth table over three arbitrary distinct input bit parents. Native never sees hidden parents or truth table. Actual step observations only.
first_use: Frozen new seed-indexed worlds FIT 111..114, CHECK 211..212, DEV 311..314. Every world receives 192 distinct seeded random public initial-state interventions for each action, globally interleaved across all worlds and actions, before unknown heldout chains length3/5. One source outcome per 192 input states per action, model parameters fixed before composed DEV labels.
native: For each action and output bit, fit a 3-parent local conditional distribution from real source rows by searching the 56 unordered parent triples, with deterministic minimum prediction error, then store the fitted 8-bin Boolean table. World-specific learning and authentically cold-restored checkpoint required.
controls: Independent exhaustive three-parent fitted conditional table, depth-3 greedy CART-style tree, 1NN on full input, original affine GF(2) fit, single-step-only ablation, world identity ablation. All use same public actions and output pairs. No native novelty from a tie.
advancement: Bounded exact terminal >=60/64 across novel 3/5-step DEV chains, >=12/16 per unseen world, and >=24 successes more than no-composition. If equally informed exhaustive model matches, do NOT assert structural novelty. More memory or CPU also vetoes Pareto improvement.
scope: An authored deterministic nonlinear causal micro-world; 192 of 256 public states per action supply near-complete system identification. This is not efficient few-shot general learning, real physics, or autonomous discovery of arbitrary semantic structure.
